title: CMC hospital working hours and outpatient OPD timings
text:
# CMC Hospital Working Hours and Outpatient (OPD) Timings
Christian Medical College (CMC) Vellore operates standard hospital services during the following hours:
- General Hospital Working Hours: Monday to Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, and Saturday from 8:00 AM to 12:30 PM.
- Outpatient (OPD) Clinics: Most specialty and general outpatient clinics conduct consultations during hospital working hours (Monday to Friday 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Saturday 8:00 AM to 12:30 PM).
- Department Schedules: Specialty clinics (such as Cardiology, Nephrology, Rheumatology, Obstetrics, and Orthopaedics) have designated consulting days. Prior appointment booking via the CMC Patient Portal is required before your in-person appointment.
- Hospital Cash and Billing Counters: Open from 7:00 AM across OPD blocks to facilitate early morning registration and bill settlement.
- Helpdesk and Patient Call Centre: Monday to Saturday from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, and Sunday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM via phone +91 8000338855 or callcentre@cmcvellore.ac.in.

title: CMC emergency department trauma care and ambulance services
text:
# CMC Emergency Care and Ambulance Services
CMC Vellore provides round-the-clock emergency medical services:
- 24/7 Emergency Medical Services (EMS): The Emergency Department at the Town Campus operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year for urgent, acute, and life-threatening conditions.
- Ranipet Campus Level 1 Trauma Care: The Kannigapuram campus on NH 46 features a state-of-the-art Level 1 Trauma Center operational 24/7 for severe trauma, poly-trauma, and road traffic accident emergencies.
- Emergency Ambulance Services: The CMC ambulance helpline is reachable 24 hours a day at +91 9791979797.
- Patient Related Helplines: For urgent patient coordination, call +91 8000338855, WhatsApp +91 9385285928, or email callcentre@cmcvellore.ac.in.

title: CMC appointment consultation fees and payment rates
text:
# CMC Appointment Consultation Charges and Payment Rates
CMC Vellore revised official consultation rates for outpatient visits:
## Private Patient Rates
- New appointment (First visit to CMC without a hospital number, includes consultation fee and Hospital Number Card): Rs. 990/-
- Repeat appointment to same unit consultant within 90 days (3 months): Rs. 470/-
- New appointment or first visit to a different unit or department (by referral or choice): Rs. 900/-
- Repeat appointment to the new department within 90 days: Rs. 470/-
- Renewal repeat appointment after 3 months (90 days): Rs. 900/-
## General Patient Rates
- New General appointment (First visit to General OPD, includes Patient ID card and consultation): Rs. 350/-
- Repeat General appointment (Same unit or different unit): Rs. 230/-
## Payment Methods
Online via Net Banking, Debit/Credit Card, UPI on the CMC Patient Portal, or cash/card at hospital billing counters.

title: CMC appointments and online services
text:
# CMC Online Appointments and Booking Procedure
Appointments and online payments are available through the official CMC patient portal at https://clin.cmcvellore.ac.in/ and https://www.cmcvellore.ac.in/patient-portal/.
- Booking Procedure: Use the 'Make online appointment' link to enter the booking system. Select consultation type (General or Private) and desired department.
- Pre-Registration for Indian Patients: First-time Indian visitors can complete their sociological details online to obtain a confirmation number.
- Registration Verification Counters: Take your confirmation number to Silver Gate (counter 600) for Private appointments, or ISSCC Building (counters 2, 3, 4) for General appointments.
- MediAgent Limitation: MediAgent provides verified public guidance and cannot book appointments or inspect live slot availability.

title: CMC booking changes unit transfer and refund rules
text:
# CMC Online Appointment Changes and Refund Policy
Q: If I book a wrong appointment online, will it be refunded?
A: Appointments booked online will not be refunded as per CMC's official hospital policy. Verify doctor and department details before making payments.

Q: Is it possible to change the appointment date?
A: Yes, a onetime postponement or advancement of appointment date is permitted online through the patient portal.

Q: Can I change the unit or department of an online appointment?
A: Changing the unit or department of an online appointment is not possible. A new appointment must be booked for the desired department.

Q: Whom should I contact for online booking issues?
A: Contact webappointment@cmcvellore.ac.in or call +91 8000338855 for online booking and transaction queries.

title: CMC appointment preparation identification and registration rules
text:
# CMC Appointment Preparation and Photo Identification
- Mandatory Government Photo ID: All patients and accompanying persons must present a valid government-issued photo identity proof (such as Aadhaar card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence) at the OPD entrance and registration desks.
- Existing Hospital Number: Patients who have previously visited CMC must use their permanent Hospital Number rather than registering as a new patient.
- Single Hospital Number: A Hospital Number is a continuing permanent medical record. Do not create separate hospital numbers for different medical specialties.
- Warning Against Touts and Outside Agents: CMC has no authorized outside booking agents, middlemen, or service centers. Never pay money to anyone outside official CMC counters.

title: CMC outpatient advance OPAD and hospital number card
text:
# CMC Hospital Number Card and Outpatient Advance (OPAD)
Q: What is a Hospital Number Card?
A: The Hospital Number Card is a permanent patient identity smart card used for all medical records, payments, and clinic visits across CMC Vellore campuses.

Q: What is OPAD (Outpatient Advance)?
A: OPAD is an advance deposit facility linked to your Hospital Number Card. Depositing funds into OPAD allows doctors to order lab tests, scans, and medications that are charged directly without having to stand in cash counter queues.

Q: Can I refund leftover OPAD balance?
A: Yes, unused advance balances in OPAD can be refunded at payment counters upon completion of your visit.

Q: What should I do if my Hospital Number Card is lost?
A: Report immediately to Payment Counters or Silver Gate to block the lost card and request a replacement.

title: CMC eMeds prescriptions by post and home delivery
text:
# CMC eMeds: Prescriptions by Post and Courier
Q: How can I order CMC medicines by post?
A: Registered CMC patients can log into the CMC Patient Portal or CMC Mobile App, view valid outpatient prescriptions, and pay online. Medicines are dispatched by postal mail or courier.

Q: What payment modes are accepted for eMeds?
A: Payment can be completed online using Debit/Credit cards or Net Banking.

Q: Can all medicines be delivered by post?
A: No, temperature-sensitive cold chain medications (such as insulin or vaccines) cannot be dispatched by post or courier.

Q: How can I track my eMeds package?
A: A postal tracking consignment number is sent by SMS to the patient's registered mobile number once dispatched.

title: CMC international patients pre-registration and IRO guidelines
text:
# CMC International Patients and International Relations Office (IRO)
CMC Vellore welcomes international patients through the International Relations Office (IRO):
- Mandatory IRO Registration: All international patients must register in person at the IRO office upon arrival in Vellore before seeing any doctor or booking outpatient clinics.
- Required Documents: Original Passport, valid Indian Medical Visa (or Medical Attendant Visa for companions), sponsor/embassy letters (if applicable), and prior medical reports in English.
- Medical Visa Invitation Letters: International patients requiring visa invitation letters can request them online through the CMC Patient Portal by submitting relevant medical summaries.
- IRO Contact: Reachable through the main CMC telephone lines or the patient call centre at +91 8000338855.

title: CMC 7 campuses network and campus guide
text:
# CMC Vellore Campuses Network and Campus Guide
CMC Vellore operates healthcare, training, and research across seven distinct campuses:
- Town Campus (Established 1924): Located on Ida Scudder Road, Vellore 632004. Primary quaternary care teaching hospital housing major medical and surgical specialties, outpatient departments, and central emergency.
- Ranipet Campus (Kannigapuram): Located on NH 46 Chennai-Bengaluru highway. Advanced multi-specialty hospital featuring a Level 1 Trauma Care Center, multi-organ transplants, and comprehensive cancer care.
- Bagayam Campus: Located in Bagayam, Vellore. Houses the Mental Health Centre (MHC), Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PMR) Institute, and Community Health and Development (CHAD) hospital.
- Kagithapattarai Campus: Educational campus housing the College of Nursing and Allied Health Sciences.
- Chittoor Campus: Secondary multi-specialty care hospital located in Andhra Pradesh.
- Schell Eye Hospital (Established 1901): Dedicated specialty ophthalmology center located in Vellore.
- RUHSA (Rural Unit for Health and Social Affairs): Community medicine and rural outreach program located in K.V. Kuppam block.

title: CMC insurance and cashless ACCESS services
text:
# CMC ACCESS Cashless Insurance Guidelines
ACCESS coordinates health insurance and corporate cashless coverage at CMC Vellore:
- Campus Locations: Town Campus ACCESS is located at Room 603 (Phone: +91 416 2283604 / 6193, Email: care_preauth@cmcvellore.ac.in). Ranipet Campus ACCESS is at Room A004 (Phone: +91 4172 224102 / 104, Email: access.rpt@cmcvellore.ac.in).
- Cashless Policy Restriction: Cashless hospitalization is strictly available for eligible inpatient admissions. Outpatient consultations, diagnostic tests, and emergency room visits are excluded from cashless claims and must be paid directly.
- Surgical Admissions: Patients scheduled for surgery must contact ACCESS at least 3 days prior to admission for preauthorization processing.
- Required Documentation: Valid government photo ID, health insurance policy card / e-card, employer ID (for corporate policies), and doctor's admission recommendation note.

title: General cough education
text:
# Overview of Cough
A cough has many possible causes, and a chatbot cannot identify the cause for an individual.

# Red Flags and Urgent Care
Seek urgent medical assessment for a rapidly worsening or very bad cough, chest pain, difficulty breathing, coughing up blood, or blue lips.

# When to Consult a Clinician
Consult a clinician if a cough lasts more than three weeks or is accompanied by persistent high fever, unexplained weight loss, or difficulty swallowing. This is general education, not a diagnosis or a substitute for local care.

title: Paracetamol and acetaminophen general medicine information
text:
# Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Information
Paracetamol is also called acetaminophen. It is an analgesic and antipyretic used to relieve mild to moderate pain and reduce fever.

# Brand Formulations and Safety
A brand name may contain the same active ingredient, but strength, formulation, and additional active ingredients can differ, so always verify the product label. Never take more than one paracetamol or acetaminophen-containing medicine at the same time to avoid risk of liver damage. This is general education, not a personal prescription or dosing instruction.

title: Dolo-650 product composition reference
text:
# Dolo-650 Active Ingredient Reference
The published Dolo-650 product reference identifies paracetamol 650 mg as its active ingredient.

# Important Clarification
Product names and formulations can change by market. Dolo is a brand name; paracetamol is the active pharmacological ingredient. Always consult a licensed healthcare practitioner or pharmacist before taking medications.

title: Cetirizine general medicine information
text:
# Cetirizine Overview
Cetirizine is a second-generation antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes, itchy nose or throat, and urticaria (hives).

# Precautions
While less sedating than first-generation antihistamines, some individuals still experience drowsiness. Check package labels and consult a pharmacist or doctor regarding personal use.

title: General fever education
text:
# Understanding Fever
A fever is a temporary elevation in body temperature, usually defined as 38°C (100.4°F) or higher. It is a natural immune response to infections such as viruses or bacteria.

# General Supportive Care
Stay well hydrated with fluids, get plenty of rest, and wear lightweight clothing.

# Red Flags and Emergency Care
Seek immediate emergency care if fever exceeds 39.4°C (103°F), lasts over 3 days, or is accompanied by severe headache, stiff neck, confusion, breathing difficulties, or an unblanching rash.

title: General headache education
text:
# Understanding Headaches
Headaches are common and most are benign, such as tension headaches or mild migraines.

# Red Flags and Immediate Medical Assessment
Seek immediate emergency care for a sudden 'thunderclap' headache (worst headache of your life), headache following head trauma, or headache accompanied by neck stiffness, confusion, fever, vision loss, or neurological weakness.

title: Ibuprofen and NSAID general medicine information
text:
# Ibuprofen and NSAIDs
Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, inflammation, and fever.

# Safety Warnings and Precautions
NSAIDs can irritate the stomach lining and are not recommended for individuals with stomach ulcers, severe kidney disease, or certain heart conditions without physician supervision. Always check labels and discuss with a pharmacist or physician before use.
